# Requirements Document: Cancelling an order

## Introduction

A seller cancels an order that has no payment at once.  An order with any
payment, full or partial, is cancelled only by accepting a cancellation offer
from the airline, priced like a change whose new price is zero.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Change/Cancel.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Change/Cancel.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet. *Sources* lists the pages each rule was written from, and *Confirmation* says whether anyone outside the model has confirmed the rule as written.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-203

**User Story:** As a seller, I want an unpaid order cancelled at once and a paid order cancelled through an offer, so that every cancellation that returns money is priced first.

**Rule:** WHEN a seller asks to cancel an order THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel it at once if no payment has been received for it, and otherwise only through a cancellation offer. (Lean: `requestCancellation`)

**Sources:** [EASD guide, Cancellation of Order Items](https://standards.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EASD/pages/574783569/Cancellation+of+Order+Items) (standard); [IATA capability ORDCA2](https://retailing.iata.org/armi/docs/ORDCA2/) (standard)

**Confirmation:** Not confirmed yet.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a seller asks to cancel an order for which no payment has been received THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel and remove at once every service of the order that the delivery status table lets be removed.
   - ONE-203.1, proven: proven theorem `unpaid_cancelled_at_once`; example `unpaidCancellation`; example `unpaidCancellationWhileRequested`
2. WHEN an order is cancelled at once THE SYSTEM SHALL mark each of its items cancelled and the order closed.
   - ONE-203.2, open: open theorem `cancelled_at_once_closed`; counterexample `unpaidCancellation`; counterexample `unpaidCancellationWhileRequested`
3. IF a seller asks to cancel an order for which any payment has been received THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL cancel it only through a cancellation offer.
   - ONE-203.3, proven: proven theorem `paid_needs_offer`; example `paidCancellation`; example `partlyPaidCancellation`
4. WHEN an order with payments is cancelled through an offer THE SYSTEM SHALL not make the amount due by the airline larger than the payments received for the order.
   - ONE-203.4, open: open theorem `offer_within_payments`; counterexample `partlyPaidCancellation`
5. WHEN an order with payments is cancelled through an offer THE SYSTEM SHALL price the cancellation from the order items that still hold a live service.
   - ONE-203.5, proven: proven theorem `offer_priced_from_live_items`; example `cancelAfterChange`

#### Open question on ONE-203.2

> An order cancelled at once has every item cancelled and is closed, under
> every reading of the guide.
>
> Open question for the business.  A cancellation removes each service through
> the delivery status table, and the table has no move to REMOVED from
> REQUESTED or from UNABLE TO DELIVER, under any reading.  A service the
> airline has not yet confirmed therefore stays REQUESTED, and its item is not
> cancelled.  The example `unpaidCancellationWhileRequested` shows it.  A
> service UNABLE TO DELIVER, such as one on a flight the airline cancelled,
> stays too, so cancelling that order never closes it.  Under the readings that
> refuse to cancel a service IN PROGRESS, or that allow delivery before
> payment, a service IN PROGRESS or already DELIVERED stays as well.  Can a
> seller cancel a service the airline is still deciding on, or one the airline
> cannot deliver, and what delivery status does it take?

#### Open question on ONE-203.4

> A cancellation offer never makes the amount due by the airline larger than
> the payments received for the order.
>
> Open question for the business.  The offer is priced from the price of the
> order's live items, as in the worked examples, and the payments received do
> not enter it.  A partly paid order is cancelled through an offer that returns
> its whole price.  The example `partlyPaidCancellation` shows it: a
> 1,000.00 order with 300.00 received gets an offer of 1,000.00 due by the
> airline.  Is the refundable amount capped at the payments received, and which
> route applies when some items are paid and others are not?
